Requirement

/rih-KWY-er-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Requirement means something that is needed or required; a necessary condition.

A current lifeguard certification is a strict requirement for anyone applying to work at the city pool this summer.

Worked Example

The scholarship listed a 3.5 GPA as its main requirement, so Dana checked her transcript carefully before spending an hour on the application.

The GPA is not a suggestion or a bonus — it is a condition that must be met before Dana is even eligible. That is exactly what a requirement is: a necessary condition standing between you and the thing you want.

How Requirement Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

prerequisite

prerequisite: a condition that must be satisfied beforehand

necessity

necessity: something one cannot do without

condition

condition: a demand that must be met for something to happen

Antonyms

option

option: a choice left entirely up to you

extra

extra: something added on but not needed

How Strong Is It? — preference → requirement → mandate

preference vs. requirement

preference vs. requirement: A preference is milder than a requirement — the hiring manager preferred bilingual candidates but did not insist on it.

mandate vs. requirement

mandate vs. requirement: A mandate is stronger than a requirement — the new safety mandate forced every factory in the state to comply immediately, with no exceptions granted.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again, back (here: intensive)

Root — quire

Root — quire: to seek, to ask (Latin quaerere)

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Put the pieces together: re- (intensively) + quire (to seek, ask) + -ment (the result of) literally builds "the result of asking insistently." What an authority keeps asking for becomes the condition you must meet — a requirement.

Use the root in a new word: inquire

Use the root in a new word: inquire: The reporter called the mayor's office to inquire — literally "to ask into" — about the missing funds.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / institutional

Requirement lives in eligibility contexts: admissions, licensing, job postings, graduation checklists. It names a condition a PERSON or application must satisfy — it is not the rule document itself. If a college "waives a requirement," the condition is dropped but the program still exists.
